title: How to Make Sure You Never Get Asked Out
request: make video for this script now (How to Make Sure You Never Get Asked Out, second version of the script)
sources: David Gale and Lloyd S. Shapley, "College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage", The American Mathematical Monthly, vol. 69, 1962. Showed that when one side does the asking, everyone ends up in pairs nobody wants to break, and every member of the asking side gets the best partner they could have in any such pairing. That the waiting side gets its worst such partner was shown soon after (D. G. McVitie and L. B. Wilson, "The Stable Marriage Problem", Communications of the ACM, 1971). As given in Biku's script.

The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2012, awarded to Alvin E. Roth and Lloyd S. Shapley for the theory of stable allocations and the practice of market design. https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2012/summary/

Alvin E. Roth and Elliott Peranson, "The Effects of the Change in the NRMP Matching Algorithm", JAMA, 1997. The US residency match switched to an applicant-proposing version, where the doctors do the asking, starting with the 1998 match.

National Resident Matching Program, "2026 Main Residency Match By the Numbers": 38,354 active applicants matched to a first-year position. Checked by Claude on 2026-10-14 against the NRMP news release "NRMP Releases Results of the 2026 Main Residency Match for More Than 38,000 Future Residents" (https://www.nrmp.org/about/news/2026/03/nrmp-releases-results-of-the-2026-main-residency-match-for-more-than-38000-future-residents/), which agrees. What the scene invents: the party, the Trainer, the woman who waves.
